title: Michael Kim Cards 15th-Ever 59 in PGA Tour History at 3M Open
dek: Michael Kim carded a 12-under 59 on Friday at the 3M Open, the 15th such score in PGA Tour history. The bogey-free round moved him to 14-under for the tournament and a three-shot lead over Ben Kohles.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Kim's 59, closed with a 24-foot putt on the 18th, is only the fourth such score on the PGA Tour since 2024.
bottom_line: Kim holds a commanding three-shot lead heading into the weekend after one of golf's rarest rounds. Watch whether he can maintain composure over 36 more holes and whether Kohles or any other chaser can close the gap on the course where he shattered his career low.
body: Michael Kim shot a 12-under 59 on Friday at the 3M Open, joining an elite group of 15 golfers who have broken 60 in PGA Tour history. The bogey-free round moved Kim to 14-under for the tournament at TPC Twin Cities and established a three-shot lead over first-round leader Ben Kohles, per ESPN.

Kim's round hinged on exceptional putting and composure down the stretch. He made five straight birdies beginning on hole 3, then added three more birdies in a four-hole stretch starting on hole 9. Eight of his 12 birdies came from putts of more than 10 feet, according to ESPN. The decisive moment came on hole 18: after his wedge from 124 yards landed pin high but rolled to the fringe, Kim faced an uphill putt from the fringe. He made the 24-foot putt to complete his round, capping four consecutive birdies to close.

Kim also made a 17-foot birdie putt on hole 17. This marks the fourth 59 shot on the PGA Tour since 2024, ESPN reported. Jake Knapp last achieved the score during the first round of the 2025 Cognizant Classic. Jim Furyk holds the PGA Tour record with a 58 at the 2016 Travelers Championship.
Kim's previous career low was a 62. He shot 69 on Thursday, making Friday's 59 a dramatic pivot. Kohles, the first-round leader, carded a 2-under 69 to reach 11-under for the tournament.

The milestone arrives after a difficult stretch. Kim missed the cut at four of his past five tournaments, including the British Open, Scottish Open, and John Deere Classic. He considered skipping the 3M Open after that stretch but spent a couple of days relaxing at home and decided to travel to the course. His lone PGA Tour win came at the 2018 John Deere Classic, and his only other recent top finish was second at the Valero Texas Open in April. In 12 tournaments since, his best finish had been 17th.
